sections.h2: A border city on the Chattahoochee
sections.html:
Phenix City sits on the Alabama bank of the Chattahoochee River, facing Columbus, Georgia. It is the seat of Russell County, and its northern and western parts reach into Lee County. The city covers about 28 square miles at 443 feet of elevation. Most of it is in the Columbus metro area, while the Lee County part falls in the Auburn metro area.

City government follows Eastern Time in practice, though the rest of Alabama uses Central Time, because the local economy is tied to Columbus. If you schedule a showing or a closing with someone on the Georgia side, confirm which clock you are both using.

ZIP codes in the city run from 36867 to 36870, and the great majority of residents live in urban areas.

Phenix City had 38,816 residents in 2020, up from 32,822 in 2010. The 2025 estimate is 38,344, a 1.2 percent drop, so the fast growth of earlier years has leveled off.

About one housing unit in ten stood empty in 2020. If your house is one of them, expect buyers to look hard at its condition, and rely on current comparable sales instead of old rankings of the city.

Phenix City depends on the larger city across the river, and many buyers and renters compare Phenix City houses with Georgia houses before they decide. A few practical points follow:

  • If you are moving to Georgia, ask the Georgia side what changes for taxes and recording there.
  • Phenix City Express runs two local bus routes that connect with METRA Transit in Columbus.
  • Chattahoochee Valley Community College is based in the city, and Troy University has a satellite campus.

An owner who relocates to Georgia for work may need to close quickly on the Alabama house, which is a common reason sellers here ask about cash.

U.S. 80 runs through the northern and western parts of the city and leads west 44 miles to Tuskegee and northeast into Columbus. U.S. 280 crosses the western part toward Opelika, 27 miles northwest. U.S. 431 runs north to south west of the city and leads south 47 miles to Eufaula. Telling buyers how close the house is to these routes helps them picture the drive.

Phenix City is humid, with rain spread through the year and about 49.1 inches falling in an average year. July highs reach 92 degrees. That wears on roofs, siding, crawl spaces and air handlers. A house that sat empty through a humid summer can develop mildew or soft wood, and inspectors flag both. If yours has been empty, air it out, run the air conditioning and fix any leak before you let anyone walk through.

Phenix City Public Schools serves the city. Because the city touches two counties, confirm with the district which schools serve an address near the Lee County line before you quote it.

Four houses in the city were added to the National Register of Historic Places on November 3, 1983: Brooks-Hughes House, Floyd-Newsome House, Morgan-Curtis House and Shapre-Monte House. If your property is one of them, ask what rules apply to exterior changes before you plan repairs.

Property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. Find out whether the current year is paid before you set a closing date.

A deed carries a state recordation tax of 50 cents per $500 of value, under Alabama Code section 40-22-1. The probate judge works it out when the deed is presented. When one deed covers land in more than one county, the probate judge certifies it to the Department of Revenue, which fixes the value in each county. That is worth knowing in a city split between Russell and Lee counties, so confirm which county your parcel is in before closing.

  • Ask which county holds the parcel record.
  • Get a written payoff for any mortgage or lien.
  • Have the closing agent prepare the proof of purchase price form.

Cash makes sense when the timeline is short or the house needs more work than you want to pay for. Common Phenix City cases:

  • A house inherited from a relative who lived in the area for decades.
  • A rental that tenants left in poor shape.
  • A vacant house that has developed humidity damage.
  • A move across the river on a set date.

How it works: you tell us about the house, and we make an offer. If you accept, a title company or closing attorney checks ownership and liens, arranges payoffs and sets the closing date. You sign, and the proceeds go to you after the mortgage and any taxes are paid.

Bring a photo ID, the deed or estate papers, mortgage payoff details and a lease if the house is rented. We buy Phenix City houses as they are. You can request an offer, compare it with a listing, and decide with no obligation.

Money owed on a property does not end the conversation. Your lender sends a payoff figure, the county supplies the tax balance, and the closing agent pays both from the sale proceeds. Anything left belongs to you.

Liens, code fines and overdue utility bills appear in the title work and are cleared the same way. In a two-county city, check that the search covers the right county records, so nothing is missed.

Behind on payments? Say so early. Buyers who pay cash can often close on a short schedule, which matters when a lender is counting days.

Ask each buyer for the offer in writing, with the closing date and who pays closing costs spelled out. Find out whether the offer depends on financing, an appraisal or an inspection. Each condition is a way for a deal to shrink or fall apart late.

Then line the offers up against a traditional listing. Subtract repairs, agent fees and the cost of carrying the house, including taxes, insurance and utilities, for however long it might sit. The best offer is the one that leaves the most money in your hands on a date you can live with.

sections.h2: Selling a house you cannot easily visit
sections.html:
Many sellers in this area live in Georgia or farther away. If you cannot be at the house, a title company can often handle signing by mail or with a notary near you. Send keys or lockbox codes by arrangement, and tell the buyer about utilities, locks and any items you want removed.

Ask for photos of the house after any work or cleanup so you know the condition on closing day. If the house is vacant, check insurance and keep the lawn mowed so the city does not issue a notice. Code notices stack up quickly on an empty house, and they become part of what must be settled at closing.

faqs.q: What county is Phenix City in?
faqs.a: Mostly Russell County, where it is the county seat. A northern and western part extends into Lee County.

faqs.q: Is Phenix City on Eastern Time?
faqs.a: In practice yes. City government follows Eastern Time because of ties to Columbus, Georgia, even though the rest of Alabama uses Central Time.

faqs.q: What river is Phenix City on?
faqs.a: The Chattahoochee River separates Phenix City from Columbus, Georgia.

faqs.q: When are Phenix City property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant or run-down Phenix City house?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as they are, including vacant and rental properties.
